thread_analysis.thread_summary: Teraoka Seiko thread for an IoT device using an Espressif module with separate Host Subsystem QDID and Controller Subsystem QDID (not a single Component QDID). Two main cases: (1) module with separate Host/Controller QDIDs requires Multi-Design registration (¥250,000), not Single-Design; (2) TCW yellow warning on the ICS Form after entering the waiver is normal — SIG approves within 1-5 US business days. The thread also documents the end-to-end registration process for this product.
all_questions_found: Our module has separate Host and Controller QDIDs. Does this mean we need Multi-Design registration?
The Review Page ICS Form shows a yellow warning after TCW entry. Will this block approval? How long does SIG take to approve?
thread_analysis.key_technical_discussion: The key determination at quoting: check the SIG qualification database to see whether the target module has a single Component QDID or separate Host/Controller QDIDs. Separate QDIDs = Multi-Design = ¥250,000. The yellow TCW indicator is the normal review state for waived inconsistencies and does not block approval. SIG's manual review window is 1-5 US business days.
thread_analysis.key_decision_logic: QDID structure determines registration type: one QDID = Single-Design; two or more QDIDs = Multi-Design. TCW = accepted known inconsistency = yellow indicator = approved by SIG after manual review, not a rejection trigger.
thread_analysis.risk_if_done_wrong: Quoting Single-Design for a module with two separate QDIDs underprices the job. Failing to enter all TCW numbers before submission causes rejection. Resubmitting during the SIG review window resets the review clock.
thread_analysis.consulting_mistake: None identified. Consultant correctly identified the Multi-Design requirement and explained the TCW yellow indicator behavior.
thread_analysis.consulting_takeaway: Always verify the QDID count of the target module before issuing a quote. One physical module can require Multi-Design registration if it has been qualified with separate Host and Controller QDIDs. This is increasingly common with modern BLE/Bluetooth module products.
